resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Status = operating, confirmed by (1) the operator's own Nov. 18, 2021 press release announcing commencement of operations, and (2) an independent March 2023 trade-press article describing Double E's 'existing system' in the context of a later expansion (Red Hills Lateral) — corroborates the pipeline was still an in-service asset well after the 2021 start. No discrepancy with the recorded value.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Fuel = Gas, confirmed by two independent sources (Summit Midstream's own commencement-of-service release and Natural Gas Intelligence's FERC-approval coverage), both stating natural gas explicitly for this named pipeline. No discrepancy.

verifications.note: "Double E is a 135 mile FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline that provides natural gas transportation services from southeast New Mexico and west Texas to downstream pipeline interconnections in the Waha Hub region" — an interstate, FERC-jurisdictional transportation (transmission-class, not gathering) pipeline; names it directly.

FERC Federal Register notice, Docket CP23-24-000: "Double E Pipeline, LLC (Double E) ... filed ... a prior notice request pursuant to sections 157.205, and 157.208 of the Commission's regulations under the Natural Gas Act (NGA) and Double E blanket certificate issued in Docket No. CP19-495-000" — an NGA/Part 157 blanket-certificate holder is by definition an interstate NGA-jurisdictional transmission pipeline (gathering lines are outside FERC's NGA jurisdiction); independent government source, names the pipeline directly.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded PipelineType = transmission, confirmed: the operator's release describes FERC-regulated interstate gas transportation service, and FERC's own Federal Register notice confirms Double E holds an NGA Part 157 blanket certificate (Docket CP19-495-000) — the certificate class reserved for interstate transmission pipelines. No discrepancy.

Searched hard, found no source giving 1997 as an in-service/start year for EPNG. Checked: (1) Wikipedia's full History section (fetched directly) -- covers the original mainline completion (Texas-California pipeline completed to Los Angeles, Dec. 1947, cited to American Gas Journal), the 1954-1996 Blue Flame Building headquarters period, Tennessee Gas Pipeline's acquisition BY EPNG's later parent in 1996, and Ruby Pipeline's 2010 creation -- no 1997 event appears anywhere in the article. (2) Kinder Morgan's own current Natural-Gas overview page -- no history/date content at all, present-tense description only. (3) Kinder Morgan's 2018 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, fetched directly) -- the only '1997' hit in the entire document is an unrelated line about the auditing firm ('We have served as the Company's auditor since 1997'), not a pipeline in-service date. (4) The seed FERC pipeline-code-list and EIA pipeline-projects-table citations are indexes, not dated history sources, and were not accessible in a form that would date EPNG's own in-service year specifically (EPNG's mainline long predates any FERC Form 549B code list or EIA project-tracking window). EPNG's mainline in-service year is documented elsewhere as 1947 (Wikipedia/Texas State Historical Association), which conflicts with the sheet's 1997 rather than supporting it -- but per the no-value-change rule this is not asserted as a correction, since '1997' could plausibly key off a specific expansion, FERC certificate, or corporate-restructuring event not yet located, and one online source search is not exhaustive for a specific historical fact this granular. Recommend a targeted FERC eLibrary docket search (not accessible from this environment) as the next step if this unit is revisited.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' FY2008 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2009-02; automated substring screen failed on my literal search label but I fetched and grepped the document directly and confirmed the exact sentence) states: 'Gulf Crossing's supply sources are mainly unconventional gas sources in the Barnett Shale and Caney Woodford Shale' -- an exact match to the sheet's 'Barnett Shale, Texas; Caney/Woodford Shale, Oklahoma.' The Wayback capture of Gulf Crossing's own company page (gulfcrossing.com/AboutUsGC.aspx, 2019-07-26 snapshot) independently repeats: Gulf Crossing 'provides takeaway capacity from the Barnett Shale in Texas and the Caney/Woodford Shale in Oklahoma.' I am NOT marking this independent -- both documents originate from the same corporate family (Boardwalk Pipeline Partners / its wholly-owned subsidiary Gulf Crossing describing itself), which the brief's independence rule treats as one origin (an applicant's own filing and its own website are the company's own self-description, not two distinct publishers), so tier is medium rather than high. I checked FERC's Federal Register notices (Draft/Final EIS notices, notice of application, notice of intent) for independent third-party language naming the Barnett Shale / Caney-Woodford Shale specifically -- these are short procedural notices and none contain that language (the full underlying EIS document, which likely does discuss gas supply basins, is not accessible as plain text via the Federal Register API). Natural Gas Intel's 'Gulf Crossing Pipeline Open for Business' article (a seed citation, a genuinely distinct trade-press publisher) is a soft-redirect dead end -- the live URL now serves an unrelated 2026 story, and no Wayback snapshot exists for that path (checked via both the wayback/available API and the CDX API, both returned empty), so I could not recover it as a second independent publisher. CONCERN: I could not find any source stating a $121,000,000 cost for the Gulf Crossing Pipeline, and every capital-cost figure I did find for this project is roughly 10-15x higher. Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' FY2006 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2007), announcing the project, put the *combined* cost of Gulf Crossing plus its associated Gulf South/Fayetteville-Greenville expansions at 'approximately $3.3 billion' for 2007-2009. The FY2008 10-K (filed 2009) itemizes Gulf Crossing separately in its capital-projects table: 'Gulf Crossing Project -- Estimated Total Cost $1,800 [million] -- Cash Invested through December 31, 2008 $1,403.5 [million].' That is consistent with the physical scope (approximately 357 miles of new 42-inch interstate transmission pipeline plus compression, a very large-diameter, long-haul project) -- $121 million would imply roughly $340,000 per mile of 42-inch pipe including compression, which is implausibly low for a 2007-2009-vintage 42-inch interstate line (steel/labor costs were unusually high in that period, which the 10-Ks themselves flag as a cost driver). I searched SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'Gulf Crossing' plus '121' / '121,000,000' / '$121 million' and reviewed the FY2006, FY2007, FY2008, and FY2009 Boardwalk 10-Ks directly (all fetched and grepped) -- none contains a $121 million figure tied to Gulf Crossing; the closest analogous number is Boardwalk's Southeast Expansion project (a different, smaller project) at $775 million estimated cost, still far above $121 million. I also checked whether $121 million could be a partial transaction value (e.g., proceeds from Boardwalk's disclosed but apparently unconsummated plan to sell a 49% interest in Gulf Crossing to a third party) -- the 10-Ks mention that structure only in the context of the $3.3 billion aggregate figure and never state a dollar value for the 49% stake itself. WebSearch quota was exhausted for this session (both at the start and again on a later retry) so I could not run open web searches for a possible EIA/trade-press citation of $121 million; everything above came from direct API/document fetches (Federal Register API, SEC EDGAR full-text search, and the four Boardwalk 10-Ks fetched by URL). Given the sheet's own likely source population (other Boardwalk-family pipelines in this cohort, e.g. Tiger and Corpus Christi/Cheniere, show similar single-figure SegmentCost fields that sometimes don't match audited totals), this reads as a probable data-entry or unit/scope error on the sheet -- flagging for Update rather than changing the value or fabricating a citation for it.

Current operational status as of Jan 2025 is confirmed by a live EGT operational plan document posted on pipelines.energytransfer.com (dated gas day 01/09/25). None of these sources trace to GEM. CLASSIFICATION correct: Fuel=Gas, a genuine long-haul interstate transmission/storage trunk (not gathering/feeder) -- confirmed by the same SEC 10-K language ('interstate transportation and storage business') and by the system's FERC NGA jurisdiction. DUPLICATE check: compared against the full 45-row Texas-operating roster.
